title: Integrated Applied-ML Eval Playbook: Onboarding, Prompt Sets, Quantization, and Regression Triage
author: Maya Thompson
body:
Overview

Purpose: This playbook defines the integrated process and practical runbooks for bringing models into Redwood’s inference stack: model onboarding using the eval-harness, authoring and maintaining prompt sets and benchmarks, applying quantization profiles safely, and an organized regression triage workflow. The goal is repeatability: measurable quality, performance, and fast remediation when regressions occur.

Scope: Applies to all models intended for Redwood Hosted, Dedicated, or Private deployments and covers both open-source and vendor-provided checkpoints. It covers pre-serve validation (onboarding), ongoing quality monitoring (benchmarks & guardrails), quantization qualification, and regression handling.

Terminology
- Eval harness: the automated test suite and tooling used to run prompt sets, metrics, and regression checks.
- Prompt set: curated inputs + expected behavior/acceptance criteria used to measure quality changes.
- Quantization profile: named configuration describing bit-widths, per-channel/per-tensor choices, and kernel fallbacks used during model compilation.
- Regression: any measurable degradation in a monitored metric (quality, latency, cost) beyond defined thresholds.

Ownership and Roles
- Model owner: primary engineer responsible for the model onboarding ticket and follow-up fixes.
- Applied ML team: maintains eval harness, prompt-set catalog, and triage coordination.
- Runtime & infra: responsible for quantized build pipeline, perf benchmarking, and capacity validation.
- Product / Customer Success: provides functional acceptance criteria for customer-facing tasks.

Onboarding checklist (high-level)
1. Create onboarding ticket in the Applied ML queue with: model source, expected use-cases, target latency/cost SLOs, and responsible owner.
2. Add model to eval-harness config: name, commit/ref, tokenizer, input-output contract, and sample prompt groups.
3. Run baseline evaluation (unquantized):
   - Unit tests: tokenization round-trip, prompt/response smoke tests.
   - Quality suite: run canonical prompt sets (semantic similarity, correctness, safety checks).
   - Performance suite: p50/p95 latency on typical sequence lengths (32, 128, 512), peak throughput, memory usage.
4. Record baseline metrics in the model manifest and link to CI artifacts (eval logs, traces, artifacts).
5. Create canary deployment plan and guardrail thresholds (see sections below).

Eval harness integration (practical steps)
- Standardized config fields (example):
  - model_id: "redwood/model-x-v1"
  - tokenizer: "hf/tokenizer-x"
  - prompt_groups: ["smoke", "safety", "domain-specific"]
  - metrics: ["semantic_similarity", "exact_match", "perplexity", "hallucination_rate"]
- Runbook: to execute the harness locally/CI:
  - CI trigger: push to model onboarding branch -> workflow `eval-harness/orchestrate` runs.
  - Local: `python -m eval_harness.run --config configs/model-x.yaml --output artifacts/model-x/baseline.json`
  - Expected outputs: summary JSON, per-prompt example traces, metric breakdown CSV.
- Acceptance gate: all critical prompt groups must pass the defined acceptance criteria (see Prompt Sets). If any fail, provide triage notes and a remediation plan before canary.

Prompt sets & benchmarks (guidelines)
- Catalog & ownership: every prompt set must have an owner, a short description, example inputs, expected outputs/labels, and acceptance criteria. Store in `prompt-sets/` with a manifest that links to downstream monitoring.
- Types of prompt sets:
  1. Smoke: fast checks (50–200 prompts) for tokenization, format, and obvious regressions.
  2. Functional: domain-specific correctness (500–2000 prompts).
  3. Safety: adversarial/safety cases (100–500 prompts).
  4. Regression: curated failing cases that historically break across versions (as small as 20–100 prompts).
- Metrics to record per prompt set:
  - Semantic similarity (sentence-transformer cosine): target >= 0.78 for parity with baseline unless product owner approves lower.
  - Exact match / classification accuracy for structured tasks: delta vs baseline <= 1.5 percentage points.
  - Hallucination rate (human-labeled or heuristic): target < 3% for knowledge-critical tasks.
  - Safety violation count: 0 allowed for restricted categories; must be investigated immediately.
- Benchmark cadence: run functional + safety suites on every model commit and nightly for production models. Regression sets run on every canary roll.

Quality guardrails and rollout gates
- Define SLOs at model level (examples):
  - Latency: p50 < 100ms, p95 < 300ms for 128-token sequences on Dedicated hardware profile A.
  - Cost-per-1k-tokens budget: track and alert if > 20% above baseline after quantization.
  - Semantic-quality: semantic_similarity delta <= -0.02 vs baseline (absolute or relative thresholds as appropriate).
- Gate types:
  1. Blocker gate: any safety violation or >5% absolute drop in critical accuracy blocks rollout.
  2. Alert-only gate: small quality regressions or cost increases create alerts for manual review but do not automatically block.
  3. Canary auto-rollback: if runtime monitors detect sustained regression beyond threshold for 10 minutes or X% of requests, auto-rollback to last known-good model.
- Monitoring signals to integrate: eval-harness short-run outputs, runtime telemetry (latency, OOMs, error rates), downstream customer errors, manual reports.

Quantization profiles and qualification playbook
- Profile naming: use stable, descriptive names (e.g., `q4_0-perchannel-kernelA`, `q3b-pertensor-kernelB`). Store profiles in `quantization-profiles/` with documented expected benefits and known tradeoffs.
- Qualification steps for each profile:
  1. Functional parity test (eval-harness): run the same prompt sets as baseline; record metric deltas.
  2. Performance test: measure latency and throughput on target hardware (3 perf runs, median reported).
  3. Memory and stability: run sustained load test for 6 hours at target throughput to catch memory leaks/accumulated errors.
  4. Fallback validation: ensure runtime can route to higher-precision kernels if per-token failure observed.
- Acceptance criteria for production-use quantization profile:
  - Semantic similarity delta >= -0.02 (unless explicitly approved by product).
  - No new safety violations introduced.
  - Latency improvement >= 15% or memory reduction >= 30% (select one or both depending on objective).
- Example CLI for building quantized artifact: \
```
./build_quantized.sh --model model-x --profile q4_0-perchannel-kernelA --out artifacts/model-x/q4_0/
```
- Document known model-specific caveats in the profile manifest (e.g., excessive nans on specific attention kernels).

Regression triage playbook (when a regression alert fires)
1. Detection: alerts can originate from: nightly eval runs, canary monitors, customer reports, or automated regression sets. Each alert must include: metric name, delta vs baseline, affected prompt examples, timestamps, and environment (canary/production).
2. Initial responder (Applied ML on-call): acknowledge within 30 minutes. Create a triage ticket and tag `regression` + model id.
3. Triage steps (first 60 minutes):
   - Re-run failing prompt(s) against baseline artifact (unquantized) + current artifact to confirm.
   - Capture full trace: token-level logits, attention maps (if available), and runtime logs.
   - Check recent changes: model weights, tokenization changes, quantization profile, runtime kernel upgrades.
4. Prioritization rubric:
   - Sev-1: safety violations, data-exfiltration/hallucination leading to user harm, or 10%+ drop in core accuracy.
   - Sev-2: 3–10% drop in non-critical accuracy, moderate latency regressions affecting SLAs.
   - Sev-3: small deltas (<3%) or isolated issues.
5. Remediation paths:
   - Rollback to previous model tag (fast path) if regression is severe and cannot be remediated quickly.
   - Patch model: adjust decoding params, temperature, or small fine-tune if bug is model-internal.
   - Rebuild with alternative quantization profile or kernel.
   - If caused by infra/runtime change, coordinate with runtime team for hotfix or rollback.
6. Post-incident actions:
   - Root cause analysis document inside the incident ticket.
   - Add failing examples to the regression prompt set and lock with a maintainer.
   - If appropriate, add automated test to the eval-harness CI for future prevention.

Release & rollout procedures
- Canary plan template: 1% traffic for 30 min -> 5% for 60 min -> 25% for 2 hours -> 100% if no critical alerts.
- Always run the regression prompt set on canary traffic in parallel. If any blocker gate fires: immediate rollback.
- Communication: update release notes with changes to model, quantization profile, expected perf/cost delta, and link to eval artifacts.

Appendix: templates & commands
- Eval-harness run (CI): `python -m eval_harness.run --config configs/model-x.yaml --groups smoke,functional,safety --out artifacts/model-x/eval.json`
- Canary rollback command (example): `redwoodctl rollout rollback --service model-serving --model model-x --to-tag model-x@2026-11-12`
- Perf script sample: `./perf_runner --model artifacts/model-x/q4_0 --batch-sizes 1,4,8 --seq-lens 32,128,512 --runs 5`
